overview: This Senate resolution marks the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II, when Japan formally surrendered aboard the USS Missouri on September 2, 1945. It honors all American veterans of the war in both the Pacific and European theaters and thanks them for their service. It also mourns those killed in the Battle of Okinawa, reaffirms the 1951 peace treaty with Japan signed in San Francisco, and recognizes the alliances the U.S. built in the Indo-Pacific region after the war, including with Japan, Australia, the Philippines and South Korea. It calls on Americans to mark the anniversary as a day of appreciation for the World War II generation. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 10, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors the sacrifice of the World War II generation while there are still living veterans, and recognizes how postwar alliances have helped keep peace in Asia.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it doesn't change any law or provide new benefits or services for veterans.
